$comment: Session metadata pushed to originals/<slug>/_session.json in Blob Storage by scripts/apply-session-meta.mjs. Only the keys present here are written; anything else already in a session's sidecar (cover, order, date, image captions) is preserved. Titles follow 'Place, Region, Month Year' so they stay consistent and lead with the words people search for. Descriptions appear on the session page only, not on the home-page cards. Species are named only where they're unmistakable; anything uncertain stays at group level on purpose.

august-adventures-2026.title: Puget Sound, Washington, July 2026
august-adventures-2026.description: Odds and ends from a few weeks close to home. A garter snake working through a meal it had no business attempting, a millipede curled up in my palm, a flounder from a low tide. The hummingbird at the feeder finally held still.

camping-eastern-wa-july-2026.title: Eastern Washington, July 2026
camping-eastern-wa-july-2026.description: Spent most of this trip face-down in the dirt with a macro lens. Grasshoppers that disappear the moment they stop moving, robber flies working over something they'd caught, stoneflies that found the tent every night. A pair of otters came up on a log while I was packing out.

costa-rica-amphibian-research-center-cra.title: Guayacán, Costa Rica, September 2026
costa-rica-amphibian-research-center-cra.description: A night walk on the grounds of the Costa Rican Amphibian Research Center, which breeds endangered frogs for release. Wall-to-wall amphibians once it got dark. Leaf frogs out on the branch tips, glass frogs you can see straight through from below, dart frogs down in the litter. A click beetle with two glowing spots, and a cicada halfway out of its old shell.

costa-rica-bijagua-august-2026.title: Bijagua, Costa Rica, August 2026
costa-rica-bijagua-august-2026.description: The feeders here pull hummingbirds in all morning, and I spent most of it sitting still. Several species working the same patch of verbena, a couple of them iridescent enough to change colour as they turned. Toucans in the fruiting trees overhead and big orb-weavers strung between the branches.

costa-rica-el-zota-biological-station-se.title: El Zota Biological Station, Costa Rica, September 2026
costa-rica-el-zota-biological-station-se.description: Lowland Caribbean rainforest, and the trails gave up more than I expected for a few days' work. Motmots and trogons sitting dead still in the understory, a toucan high up in the canopy, basilisks along the creek. Dart frogs underfoot the whole time. Bats roosting in a culvert on the walk back.

costa-rica-la-fortuna-arenal-august-2026.title: Arenal Volcano, Costa Rica, September 2026
costa-rica-la-fortuna-arenal-august-2026.description: Arenal showed its cone for about an hour before the clouds closed in again, which I gather is normal. Most of these are from the night walks instead. Tree frogs asleep with their eyes shut, big wandering spiders out hunting, a coati working the trail edge at first light.

costa-rica-monteverde-natural-reserve-au.title: Monteverde Cloud Forest, Costa Rica, September 2026
costa-rica-monteverde-natural-reserve-au.description: Monteverde earns the name. The mist never lifted the whole time I was there, which is the point of a cloud forest. Hanging bridges out through the canopy, a millipede longer than my hand, katydids shaped exactly like the leaves they sit on. The stream was running clear in the middle of the wet season.

costa-rica-playa-flamingo-august-2026.title: Playa Flamingo, Costa Rica, August 2026
costa-rica-playa-flamingo-august-2026.description: Short stop on the dry Pacific coast, which feels like a different country from the Caribbean side. One motmot sat out in the open long enough to photograph properly. Hermit crabs all over the driftwood and small fish holding in the tide pools. Put the rocks back where you found them.

costa-rica-tapir-valley-august-2026.title: Tapir Valley, Costa Rica, August 2026
costa-rica-tapir-valley-august-2026.description: Tapir Valley is old cattle pasture that was allowed to go back to wetland, and the frogs found it fast. The night walk is mostly frogs. Tree frogs on the undersides of leaves, glass frogs you can see the organs through, and a lot of small callers with their throats blown out like balloons.

costa-rica-tenorio-national-park-august-.title: Tenorio Volcano National Park, Costa Rica, August 2026
costa-rica-tenorio-national-park-august-.description: Most people come to Tenorio for the blue river. I spent the time looking at smaller things instead. Dart frogs on the forest floor, a sloth hanging directly over the trail, stick insects I only found because one of them moved. A weevil so crusted in lichen I nearly put my hand on it.

costa-rica-tortuguero-national-park-cana.title: Tortuguero canals, Costa Rica, September 2026
costa-rica-tortuguero-national-park-cana.description: You see Tortuguero from a boat, which makes the herons easy and everything else hard. Herons at every bend, including one with eyes far too big for its head. Anhingas drying their wings on the bank. A caiman holding dead still at the waterline, which I only spotted because the guide pointed at it.

costa-rica-tortuguero-night-walk-august-.title: Tortuguero night walk, Costa Rica, September 2026
costa-rica-tortuguero-night-walk-august-.description: Everything on a night walk is either asleep or hunting. Thin brown snakes looped between leaves on a body about as thick as a pencil. Lizards balled up on the branch tips where they roost, which is apparently how you find them. Katydids doing a convincing dead-leaf impression, and a scorpion down in the litter.

eastern-washington-camping-memorial-week.title: Shrub-steppe, Eastern Washington, May 2026
eastern-washington-camping-memorial-week.description: Sagebrush country, with a snow-capped volcano on the horizon all weekend. Horned lizards flattened against the basalt where you'd never pick them out. Orange butterflies working the wet gravel, quail trotting down the road ahead of the car, and a scorpion under a rock after dark.

gunn-peak-june-2026.title: Gunn Peak, Washington, June 2026
gunn-peak-june-2026.description: Gunn Peak is steep, brushy and off-trail, and there's no gentle way up it. The reward is a pair of tarns just under the summit block that go dead flat in the morning, with the tower reflected in them. Not a casual hike. Bring navigation and expect to use your hands.

july-macro-eastern-washington.title: Eastern Washington macro, July 2026
july-macro-eastern-washington.description: Macro lens, and a lot of turning over rocks. An alligator lizard working through a grasshopper headfirst, robber flies paired up on a stem, a scorpion that sat in my hand longer than I expected. Stoneflies on everything once the sun went down. Roll the rocks back the way you found them.

june-nearby-seattle-wildlife.title: Near Seattle, Washington, June 2026
june-nearby-seattle-wildlife.description: An old gravel pit twenty minutes from the city, which turns out to be the best lizard habitat I know of. They sun themselves on the broken concrete and let you get close. Banana slugs along the wet edges, a beetle down in the rubble, and a couple of crows keeping an eye on all of it.

june-sauk-mtn-and-nearby.title: Sauk Mountain, Washington, June 2026
june-sauk-mtn-and-nearby.description: Sauk Mountain is a couple of miles of tight switchbacks up an open meadow face above the Skagit, and the green was in full swing. A volcano on the skyline from the summit ridge, a lake straight down the back side, and a marmot that held its pose on the rocks long enough.

king-tide-june-2026.title: Deception Pass, Washington, June 2026
king-tide-june-2026.description: A summer king tide pulls the water back far enough to walk onto ground that's normally well under. Anemones closed up out of the water, hermit crabs, chitons clamped down hard on the rock. Bull kelp laid out flat across the cobble. Put everything back where you found it.

late-winter-washington-hikes-and-birds-2.title: Western Washington, March 2026
late-winter-washington-hikes-and-birds-2.description: March is the gap between the winter ducks and the spring migrants, so I took whatever turned up. A merganser with its crest all the way up, a bluebird out on the east side, a meadowlark singing from a young fir. A creeper working its way up a mossy trunk, which is the only way I ever spot them.

lijiang-may-2026.title: Tiger Leaping Gorge, Yunnan, April 2026
lijiang-may-2026.description: Two days on the high trail through Tiger Leaping Gorge, with snow peaks on one side, more on the other, and the river a long way down. The stretch of switchbacks in the middle is the part that hurts. Goats on ground I wouldn't walk across. A centipede and a big wolf spider on the path.

may-ball-mountain-weekend.title: Ball Mountain, Washington, May 2026
may-ball-mountain-weekend.description: Late May still meant walking on snow most of the day, and the summit stayed socked in. A pika on a mossy boulder made up for it. A red-headed woodpecker in the alders, a waterfall coming straight off the rock, and snails out everywhere in the wet.

may-tidepooling-and-animals.title: Puget Sound tide pools, Washington, May 2026
may-tidepooling-and-animals.description: Good spring low tide. Sculpins and eel-shaped fish wedged into the shallow pools, crabs with purple-tipped claws, and one crab wearing most of a barnacle bed on its back as camouflage. An osprey worked the shoreline overhead the whole time. Always put the rocks back.

mt-everest-may-2026.title: Everest north face, Tibet, May 2026
mt-everest-may-2026.description: The Tibetan side gives you the north face straight on, which is the view you don't get from Nepal. I watched it clear and cloud back over through the afternoon, then catch the last light right at sunset. The survey marker at the viewpoint reads 8,848.86 metres.

north-cascades-july-2026.title: Washington Pass, North Cascades, July 2026
north-cascades-july-2026.description: Those twin spires you see from the highway at the pass look better still from the meadows underneath them. Clear July day with water running through the meadow grass. A small toad turned up on the trail on the way back down.

olympic-winter-2026.title: Olympic National Park, Washington, February 2026
olympic-winter-2026.description: February on the peninsula means fog, rain, and almost nobody else around. Ducks and shorebirds along the strait, elk grazing out in the open. The footbridge over the narrows at the lake, and moss hanging off everything in the rain forest.

shanghai-city-and-birds-spring-2026.title: Shanghai, China, May 2026
shanghai-city-and-birds-spring-2026.description: Nights on the Bund looking across at the towers, mornings in the city parks looking at birds. There's more going on in those parks than you'd think once you start paying attention. Thrushes and bulbuls in the hedges, dragonflies over the water, and a swallowtail that wouldn't settle.

spring-pnw-various-wildlife-2026.title: Western Washington, April 2026
spring-pnw-various-wildlife-2026.description: First warm weekends of the year, when everything comes out at once. Lizards on sun-warmed rock, garter snakes in the grass, a chorus frog, a newt walking across the trail, a salamander under a log. Please never handle salamanders with bug-sprayed or lotioned hands, and put the log back the way it was.

sunrise-rainier-july-2026.title: Sunrise, Mount Rainier National Park, July 2026
sunrise-rainier-july-2026.description: Sunrise is the highest you can drive in the park, and the glacier fills most of the view from the ridge trail. I started in fog down in the meadows and walked out the top of it about an hour up. Shaggy mane mushrooms collapsing into ink on the way back down.

tibet-spring-2026.title: Tibetan plateau, China, April 2026
tibet-spring-2026.description: Lhasa first, then west over a series of passes. The Potala Palace, high lakes still half frozen, and gulls that have no business being that far inland. Yaks strung out across a snowfield, a glacier sitting right beside the road, grazing animals out on the open plateau. Everything is at altitude and the weather turns in minutes.

various-april-wildlife-2026.title: Puget Sound, Washington, April 2026
various-april-wildlife-2026.description: Half tide pools, half sun-warmed driftwood. Sea stars, small fish wedged into the damp, shrimp, and a crab riding around on top of a sea star. Fence lizards doing push-ups on the logs just above the tideline.

zhangjiajie-april-2026.title: Zhangjiajie, Hunan, April 2026
zhangjiajie-april-2026.description: The sandstone pillars at Wulingyuan are the ones people know from Avatar, and they hold mist most of the morning. Tianmen Mountain is the other half of this trip: the cable car, the switchback road, and the staircase up through the arch. There's a monorail train shaped like a pig, which I did not expect
